automatic_input.description: The entire attach path accepts AUTOMATIC_INPUT (kind 6). Absent means use DATA.

channel.description:
Stream channel: first paint, then live bytes. Send keys as DATA on it;
RESIZE, FOCUS, FACTS, CREDIT and CLOSE frames control it.

focus_by_use.description:
With `focus_updates`: the owner sizes by use (`focus_by_use`): the
viewer used last leads, so WINDOW_FOCUS(1) on each use (a touch, a
resume) matters. Absent: false (older owner: focused desktop first).

focus_updates.description: True only when every core on the path accepts WINDOW_FOCUS (kind 8).

resize_history.description:
The `resize_history` the owner applies, 0 unless every core on the
path has the `resize_history` feature (and `resize_notifications`
holds). Absent: 0.

resize_notifications.description:
True only when the entire path sends RESIZE before replacement paints.
False or absent means the viewer must track size changes separately.

visibility_updates.description: True only when every core on the path accepts viewer visibility updates.

id.description: Permanent random id, reset only when state is wiped.

name.description: Display name, the hostname by default.

Display.description: What a viewer's own terminal looks like, reported by the client.

version.description: Zero when never written. Deletions retain their version.

DraftAuthor.description: The viewer that typed into a draft last.

connection_id.description: As in `hc viewers`: the connection and channel it typed on.

peer.description: Its peer's name, when it typed through another machine.

DraftView.description: A person's draft that agents' text waits for (`hc get`, `hc viewers`).

by.description: The viewer that typed into it last; null if unknown.

chars.description:
The characters it holds, as the core followed the keys; null when it
can't tell (anything but plain text and backspaces went in): then only
sending or clearing it (Enter, ctrl+c, ctrl+u) ends it, or expiry.

expires_in_ms.description:
Ms until it expires and agents' text goes in again: after
`HC_DRAFT_IDLE_MS` (10 min) with nobody typing on the terminal, or
`HC_DRAFT_LEFT_MS` (1 min) after the viewer that typed it detached
with no viewer left.

input_ms_ago.description: Ms since a person last typed on this terminal.

since_ms.description: When the person began typing it, ms since the epoch.

old.description: Exact text, found exactly once in the file as it was.

code.description: Its exit code; null when a signal ended it.

ms.description: How long it ran, in milliseconds.

stderr.description: What it wrote, base64: the first 1 MB.

stdout.description: What it wrote, base64: the first 8 MB.

timed_out.description: It ran out of time and was ended: the output is what came so far.

truncated.description: It wrote more than was kept (it still ran to its end).

first.description: The first and last line given (last < first: none).

text.description: The lines as they are in the file, line ends kept.

started.description: Whether the agent started working on it (see terminal.send).

turn.description: The turn when it went in (see terminal.send).

cwd.description: Its working directory now (resolved by the OS).

name.description: Its name as the OS has it (`node`, `vim`, `sh`).

current.description: Same build as the core: takes new terminals. Others drain.

channel.description:
Framed mode: the channel they arrive on. Plain mode: none; this
connection now carries only notifications.

messages.description:
Messages waiting, oldest first. With follow, new ones then arrive as
`event` notifications of type `message` (data: one message).

cols.description: Initial terminal width in columns (at least 1).

rows.description: Initial terminal height in rows (at least 1).

key.description: The key sent: esc for programs that report status, else ctrl+c.

outcome.description:
stopped (left working, or a shell got its prompt back), exited,
still_working (no change in time), or unknown (it doesn't report status).

warning.description:
The core could not save its terminals just now (a full disk, say) and
keeps trying; this call itself went through, so don't repeat it.

machines.description:
Machines added here and their lines: one that is not connected is
listed here, not waited on.

terminals.description: This machine's terminals, then each connected machine's (`machine/t7`).

host.description: What that core calls itself (its hostname).

name.description: What this core calls it: `rohan` in `rohan/t7`.

session.description: The hc session there (null: its default).

target.description: How it is reached: an ssh target, or (`via`) a command.

temporary.description:
Short-lived (a sandbox for a task): clients may show it apart from the
machines that stay. hc treats it like any other.

version.description: Its hc version when last seen.

via.description:
`target` is a command that runs a shell line there, given as its last
argument, like ssh (a provider's own CLI, ssh with its options).

build.description: Identity from the live hello, absent for old or disconnected peers.

name.description: What this core calls it: `rohan` in `rohan/t7`.

session.description: The hc session there (null: its default).

since_ms.description: Since when it is not connected (ms since the epoch).

target.description: How it is reached: an ssh target, or (`via`) a command.

from.description: The sending terminal (`t3`, `machine/t3`); null for a person, a script or a note.

id.description: Counts up from 1 per terminal and is never reused, across restarts too.

text.description: The text as it would have been typed (with its `<hc>` tag).

ts.description: When it was queued, ms since the epoch.

path.description: Where it landed, as the terminal's machine sees it.

complete.description: False when part of what was asked for may be missing.

how.description: "screen", "history", or "stitched" (a full-screen app, read by scrolling it).

incarnation.description:
The program's incarnation when the text was read, under the same lock
as the text. Absent for a terminal that never started a program.

truncated.description: `max_bytes` cut the text: older lines were dropped.

why.description:
Why only the screen: "working", "blocked" or "error" (a full-screen app
is not scrolled in these states).

address.description: `t7`: this terminal forever on this core.

ctx.description:
`<nonce of this core process>-<counter>`: moves when a person or an
agent types into it (`send`, `keys`, a viewer's real input, never a
terminal's own replies), when its program's status report changes
(state, kind, message, title; not the terminal title, not progress)
and whenever a program starts. In memory only: a core restart gives a
new one (the saved value is never read back).

draft.description: `terminal.get` only: a person's unsent draft in it, which agents' text waits for (see `terminal.viewers`); absent: none. Never saved.

first_message.description: Template runs: whether the first message went in.

foreground.description: What runs in it right now and where (null once it has finished).

identity.description:
Which terminal the program believes it runs in (TERM_PROGRAM and
version), fixed at start; XTVERSION answers with it.

incarnation.description:
16 random hex characters, new each time a program is successfully
started in it (created, restarted, kept recovery). Saved. A terminal
saved by an older core gets one when this core first loads it. Null
until its first program has started.

keep.description: Replace a lost program with this machine’s shell, in place. Exit with a code and kill remain final.

notify.description: Its parent gets notes about it (see `--no-notify`).

output.description:
With `wait`: its text then, like `terminal.read` (the screen, plus
history unless it is a full-screen app).

parent.description: The terminal that started it (`t3`), set once at start.

reason.description:
Why its program ended or is pending (`spawn_pending` means its initial
spawn timed out, but the holder may still be starting it):
exited, killed, server_stop, host_shutdown (Windows
is ending the session, including logout), signaled (a kept program
died by signal without an exit code), holder_lost (its holder
died), stopped_by_restart (nothing ran it any more after a restart).

records.description: Other 7501 records by id (programs reporting on several things).

reported.description: Whether the program ever sent a 7501 report.

rm.description: Removed right after it exits (once a waiting parent has the exit code).

screen.description: "exact", or "inexact" after a core crash (older history may be missing).

status.description:
The program's own word for what it's doing (OSC 7501 root record);
null if it never said, or after it exited.

status_ms.description: When that word last changed, ms since the epoch; null if it never said.

submit.description:
Template overrides: the key that submits a message, the stop key, the pause
between paste and submit.

turn.description: Goes up each time the status leaves `working`.

wait.description: With `wait`: how the wait ended (exit, a status, or timeout: still running).

since_ms.description: When saving started to fail, ms since the epoch.

repeated.description: `terminal.queue`: its key was queued before, so it wasn't queued again.

started.description:
Whether it went `working` within a few seconds; null when it doesn't
report status, so nobody can tell.

status.description: The program's status word when the text went in (null: it never said).

turn.description: The turn when the text went in.

via.description: `typed` into its input, or queued in its `inbox` (its program follows it).

waiting.description: Queued: how many messages now wait in its inbox, this one included.

warning.description:
The core could not save its terminals just now (a full disk, say) and
keeps trying; this call itself went through, so don't repeat it.

Status.description: One 7501 record. Words are the program's own; nothing is translated.

kind.description: permission, question or auth (blocked only, when the program said).

progress.description: 0..100 (working or blocked, when the program said).

state.description: idle, working, done, blocked or error.

features.description:
What this core can do, as `hello` says (e.g. `queue`: it takes
`terminal.queue`; `queue-keyed`: with keys), so a client can choose
before it relies on one.

holder.description: The holder new terminals go to.

holders.description: Every holder: after an update, older ones run their terminals to the end.

installed_by.description:
The package manager this hc came from (homebrew, nix, mise, or
system package manager): it updates hc, `hc update` won't.
Null for a replaceable plain install.

queue_keys_kept_ms.description:
How long a terminal remembers a `terminal.queue` key: a sender may
retry a send whose answer it lost for up to this long.

saving.description:
Present while the core can't save its terminals (a full disk, say). It
keeps trying and says so here once, instead of failing calls; what
changed meanwhile is lost if the core stops before it saves.

warning.description: A restart with `force_stale_registry`: the terminals the next core will kill.

channel.description:
Framed mode: the channel events arrive on (JSON lines, with credit).
Plain mode: none; this connection now carries only notifications.

seq.description:
Events after this sequence follow. After a `missed` snapshot, ignore
events whose seq is not above the snapshot's.

terminals.description: Matching terminals here and on connected machines (`machine/t7`).

error.description: Set when the file can't be used.

contributes_to_grid.description: Included in the selected group's min-grid, or the selected fallback size.

focus_updates.description: Negotiated WINDOW_FOCUS: the viewer reports whether its window has keyboard focus.

focused.description: Its window has keyboard focus now (false without `focus_updates`).

focused_ms_ago.description: Milliseconds since its window last gained keyboard focus; null if never.

peer.description: Connected peer name for a relayed viewer; absent for local connections.

visible.description: Effective visibility; legacy clients remain visible until detach.

draft.description: A person's unsent draft, which agents' text waits for; absent: none.

focus_authority.description:
A focus-reporting viewer has been focused: only the focused (or last
focused) window may set the grid; everyone else only receives it.

selected_grid.description: What the same selector used by the live resizer currently chooses.

children.description: With `children`: one result per child it reports on.

ended.description: False on timeout: a check-in, the terminal is still running.

from.description:
With a message: the sender's address (the text is already in your input);
null when a person sent it.

or not_started (after a send: it did not start working; a plain wait
still follows that send's turn); with

wait); for each child in `children`: status, exit, or running (still
working).

status.description: The exact word the program reported (current word on timeout or output).

methods.description: Planned restart (e.g. after an update): screens are saved, programs keep running, the next core adopts them. Once asked, terminal.run and machine.exec refuse until it has restarted. It first saves its registry and waits for that: if it can't (a full disk), it refuses with `unavailable` and nothing changes, because the next core kills every terminal its registry doesn't list. `force_stale_registry` restarts anyway; the answer's `warning` names the live terminals missing from the registry saved on disk, which the next core kills.
methods.name: server.restart

params.description:
Restart even though the core can't save its terminals. The next core
then kills every live terminal missing from the registry saved on disk
(it loads that one), and the answer says which. For a restart that
can't wait, such as a disk that won't recover; otherwise free the disk.

methods.description: Paste text and press Enter, once nobody has typed for ~3 s and no draft a person typed is left unsent (it waits up to 2 min, counted from when it arrives, for them to send or clear it; a draft backspaced away is no draft, and one nobody typed on for 10 min, or whose viewer detached 1 min ago with none left, expires; terminal.get shows it as `draft`); keys a person presses meanwhile are held, then delivered. A send still waiting when its caller goes away (its `hc` was killed, its connection hung up) is dropped: nothing is typed. A client that only stops writing, as `hc connect` does when its stdin ends, still gets its answer. Refuses a blocked program unless `force`. A program that follows its inbox (terminal.inbox) gets the text queued there instead: nothing is typed. Guarded (feature `send-guarded`, with `incarnation` and `if_ctx`, and `within_ms` at most 15000, default 10000): it types only if the terminal still runs that incarnation (else `replaced`), its `ctx` is still `if_ctx` (else `context_changed`: someone typed into it, or its status report changed) and it isn't blocked (`blocked`, `force` is not allowed), and it never waits longer than `within_ms` for a person or a draft (`busy`); those four refusals type nothing. A guarded send always types, whatever follows the inbox. It holds the terminal's input from that check until its submit key: a person's keys wait and go in after it. Every write goes to the program checked; if a write fails, or anything but the paste reached the program before the submit key, it answers `unknown` and sends no submit key: the text may be sitting unsent in the program's input box, where a later Enter would submit it. Its caller leaving before it types ends it, as for any send.
methods.name: terminal.send

yet counts as working). `any`: the parent's unseen news (a turn ended, it
blocked, it hit an error, it exited), else the next child to stop working; for the parent

does not complete that task in either mode. Without a launch task, idle
still counts as stopped.
